claim: University of Michigan announced October 9 a PNAS study extracting species interactions from participatory biodiversity comments using LLMs.
verifiedFacts: The University of Michigan issued an October 9 research announcement about extracting species-interaction observations from citizen-science comments using large language models.
The university identifies a PNAS study published October 8, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2602244123, covering bird and plant-pollinator interaction extraction.
inference: A bounded ecological data-ingestion specimen could preserve observer provenance and expert corrections; extracted mentions are not unbiased population or ecological-outcome measurements.
Consultancy implication: Demonstrate traceable ecological interaction extraction with expert review and bias disclosure.
Project disposition implication: seed-loom CORE for source lineage; project-constellation INCUBATE as a domain demonstration.
significance: A direct research result connects multilingual participatory observation to measurable ecological knowledge workflows.
assumptions: Accessible comments can be used under platform terms and corrected sufficiently for a specific local ecology question.
knownLimitations: Observer, spatial and taxonomic selection bias; privacy and sensitive-species concerns.
Press release is institution-issued; full final PNAS article was not independently retrieved in this run.
